dn19:8.3: In the same way, the Buddha has well described the practice that leads to extinguishment for his disciples, and extinguishment converges with the practice.
dn19:13.6: That would be for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans!’
dn19:15.4: For this is the harbinger for the appearance of the Divinity, namely light arising and radiance appearing.
dn19:16.4: ‘We shall find out what has caused that light, and only when we have realized it shall we go to it.’
dn19:16.11: In the same way, when the divinity Sanaṅkumāra appears to the gods of the thirty-three, he outshines the other gods in beauty and glory.
dn19:17.2: In the same way, the god on whose couch the Divinity sits is overjoyed and brimming with happiness.
dn19:20.2: How the Buddha has acted for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans!
dn19:20.3: I don’t see any Teacher, past or present, who has such sympathy for the world, apart from the Buddha.
dn19:21.1: Also, the Buddha has explained the teaching well—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.
dn19:21.2: I don’t see any Teacher, past or present, who explains such a relevant teaching, apart from the Buddha.
dn19:22.1: Also, the Buddha has well described what is skillful and what is unskillful, what is blameworthy and what is blameless, what should be cultivated and what should not be cultivated, what is inferior and what is superior, and what has a portion of dark or bright.
dn19:22.2: As for one who so clearly describes all these things,
dn19:22.3: I don’t see any Teacher, past or present, with these qualities, apart from the Buddha.
dn19:23.1: Also, the Buddha has well described the practice that leads to extinguishment for his disciples. And extinguishment converges with the practice,
dn19:23.2: as the waters of the Ganges join together and converge with the waters of the Yamunā.
dn19:23.3: In the same way, the Buddha has well described the practice that leads to extinguishment for his disciples, and extinguishment converges with the practice.
dn19:23.4: I don’t see any Teacher, past or present, who so clearly describes the practice that leads to extinguishment for his disciples, apart from the Buddha.
dn19:24.1: Also, possessions and popularity have accrued to the Buddha, so much that you’d think it would thrill even the aristocrats.
dn19:24.2: But he takes his food free of vanity.
dn19:24.3: I don’t see any Teacher, past or present, who takes their food so free of vanity, apart from the Buddha.
dn19:25.1: Also, the Buddha has gained companions, both trainees who are practicing, and those with defilements ended who have completed their journey. But he sets them aside and lives committed to the joy of solitude.
dn19:25.2: I don’t see any Teacher, past or present, so committed to the joy of solitude, apart from the Buddha.
dn19:26.1: Also, the Buddha does as he says, and says as he does,
dn19:26.2: thus: he does as he says, and says as he does.
dn19:26.3: I don’t see any Teacher, past or present, who so practices in line with the teaching, apart from the Buddha.
dn19:27.1: Also, the Buddha has gone beyond doubt and got rid of indecision. He has achieved all he wished for regarding the fundamental goal of the spiritual life.
dn19:27.2: As for one who has gone beyond doubt, got rid of indecision, and achieved all he wished for regarding the fundamental goal of the spiritual life,
dn19:27.3: I don’t see any Teacher, past or present, with these qualities, apart from the Buddha.’
dn19:28.1: These are the eight genuine praises of the Buddha that Sakka proffered to the divinity Sanaṅkumāra.
dn19:30.5: “Best wishes, Jotipāla! You are summoned by King Disampati; he wants to see you.”
dn19:33.2: “Prince Reṇu, we are your friends, dear, beloved, and cherished;
dn19:33.3: we share your joys and sorrows.
dn19:33.4: King Disampati is old, elderly and senior, advanced in years, and has reached the final stage of life. Who knows how long he has to live?
dn19:33.5: It’s likely that when he passes away the king-makers will anoint you as king.
dn19:33.6: If you should gain kingship, share it with us.”
dn19:39.2: “Sir, I have got this good reputation:
dn19:39.3: ‘The Great Steward sees the Divinity in person! The Great Steward discusses, converses, and consults with the Divinity in person!’
dn19:39.4: But I don’t see the Divinity, and I don’t discuss, converse, or consult with the Divinity.
dn19:39.5: I have heard that brahmins of the past who were elderly and senior, the tutors of tutors, said:
dn19:39.6: ‘Whoever goes on retreat for the four months of the rainy season and practices the absorption on compassion sees the Divinity and discusses with him.’

dn19:53.1: “One year is too long, sirs. I cannot wait that long.
dn19:53.2: Who knows what will happen to the living?
dn19:53.3: We are headed for lives to come. We must be thoughtful and wake up! We must do what’s good and lead the spiritual life, for no one born can escape death.
dn19:53.4: As I understand what the Divinity says about putrefaction, it’s not easy to quell while living at home.
